entries.title: Fabric: pair create survives a refused push, no untested main from the prime, neutral export names
entries.brief: Retry a refused weft push and roll back the own branch, gate the prime-side push of main, rename fabric exports that carry warp/weft
entries.body:
Fabric's pushes and its exported names: pair creation survives a refused push, the prime never publishes untested `main` commits by the way, and fabric's vocabulary stays inside fabric.

## Pair creation retries a refused weft push and rolls back its own branch

From issue #433, seen 2026-10-07 when the hub started three batten runs at once (`cache-ttl-per-role`, `batcher-v2`, `burler-cost`).

- `cache-ttl-per-role`'s Worktree-Create pushed its weft branch at the same moment as the other two pairs and GitHub answered `! [remote rejected] cache-ttl-per-role-weft -> cache-ttl-per-role-weft (failed)`, with no hook message; the other two pushes went through.
- `rollbackAdd` then could not delete the warp branch: "warp-branch deletion was refused by the destructive gate (check=ownership); the branch is left behind". The branch was already pushed to origin.
- Resuming the run blocked on "branch already exists, left behind by an earlier pair", so the hub had to delete the branch locally and on the remote by hand; the next resume went through.

Wanted:

- Retry a weft push that GitHub rejects with a bare `(failed)` a few times with backoff before giving up; a bare `(failed)` reads as a transient server-side refusal.
- `rollbackAdd` removes the warp branch it created itself in the same call, locally and on the remote, instead of the ownership check refusing it.

## The prime pushes no untested main commits

Found at run-pushes' PR-Gate (PR #422), 2026-10-07; a deliberate design choice there (its Decision 5), not a defect.

In the prime, `lyx fabric push` and `sync` now push the parent branch (`main`) as well as the records side.
That includes the `sync` that `lyx config` runs after a change, which pushes whether or not the call made a commit.
So when the hub holds local `main` commits not yet pushed, a `lyx config --set` publishes them without the full `go test ./...` the hub runs before every push to `main`.

Direction: either gate the prime-side push of the parent branch (refuse, or push only the records side, when the parent branch has unpushed commits the call did not make), or keep the hub from ever holding unpushed local `main` commits.

## Fabric exports without warp/weft in their names

Seen 2026-10-04 in `pattern-init`: extending the fabric-vocabulary scan to test files outside fabric flagged 83 files, and 38 of them only name fabric's own exports that carry the words, e.g. `hubforge.Hub.PairWarpWorktree` and `WEFT_SKIP_GIT`.
`pattern-init` exempts that closed set of identifiers rather than renaming them.
Rename those exports to neutral names so the vocabulary stays inside fabric, then shrink the exemption set to nothing.

entries.title: Kick-start packs from tool locations through quarry Enclose
entries.brief: Turn file:line locations from verify failures, lint and audits into member glyphs with quarry enclose, then into a kick-start pack
entries.body:
Operator, 2026-10-08: quarry gains `Enclose`, written as quarry's task `enclose-locations` (in the quarry repo; the operator spawns it).
It maps `file:line` ranges from tool output to the innermost enclosing member glyphs, with the same Symbol data `Resolve` returns, also at a git revision (`quarry enclose [--rev R]`).
Markdown is out of its scope: a `.md` location is a per-item rejection.

Use in Loomyard once it lands, building on the kick-start pack:

- Verify failures (`go test` failure lines, `go vet`, compile errors) give the recovery agent or fixer a pack of the failing members.
- Comment-lint findings and Webster audit findings carry glyphs instead of lines.
- A review finding that cites `path:line` despite the glyph rule is mapped at the reviewed revision, then resolved in the working tree, so the fixer's own edits never shift it.

Glyph↔path conversion stays in quarry; Loomyard never intersects lines with symbol spans itself.

## Quarry's Enclose as delivered (quarry PR #36, 2026-10-08)

- Released in quarry v0.3.0: `(*Repo).Enclose(locs)` and `(*Repo).EncloseAt(rev, locs)`, with `EncloseResult`, `EncloseReasons` and `RenderEncloseJSON`; paths are relative to the repo root, not the cwd, and an unknown rev fails the whole call.
- They take location spellings (`path:N`, `path:N-M`, `path:N:col`), not structs; Loomyard formats tool-output locations into them.
- Rejections carry a closed reason set (`EncloseReasons`), including `unaddressable` for a `.go` file in the repo root or a path containing `#`; Loomyard cites `path:line` for any rejected item.
- A `found` glyph may not Resolve afterwards (an explicitly named gitignored file, a file without a package clause, a path through a symlinked directory; `quarry/enclose.go`). Loomyard treats a Resolve miss after Enclose as "no current span", never as an error, the same as a member the fixer deleted or renamed.
- Loomyard pins quarry v0.2.1; this task bumps `go.mod` to v0.3.0, which has no other breaking change.

entries.title: Shuttle: one session-state model, held turns as waits, stuck not a question, a deliberate permission setup
entries.brief: Shuttle computes busy/idle-done/idle-stalled/asking/dead from hooks in shadow mode, holds show as waits, a stuck outcome is classified from its file, and the hook denies python
entries.body:
Shuttle reads what an agent session is doing from what Claude Code reports, and the stops built on that reading stop misfiring.

## One session-state model

Decided in direction by the operator 2026-10-07: unify how lyx knows what an agent session is doing, owned by shuttle.

## Why

Every module guesses an agent's state its own way, and each guess has failed:

- Batten judges a run quiet from the child's status file, which changes only at a step's end; on 2026-10-07 an API error stalled all five runs and the quiet notices came 45 min later, long after the agents were resumed by hand, naming no cause.
- The orch watcher runs its own idle probe and reads turn ends, and its compact cycle missed its own compaction (`orch-compact-timeout`).
- Shuttle's turn reading misses Stops and waits on finished background shells (#411, #420; `shuttle-turns`).
- An injected text races the operator's typing between the idle probe and the Enter (see `creel`).
- Nothing notices a live session stopped by an API error, machine sleep or a dropped network; elapsed time and transcript growth cannot tell it apart from a long simulation or test run.

## Direction

Shuttle owns one session-state model per agent strand, and batten, the orch watcher, creel and reed read it instead of inferring their own:

- `busy`: a turn is running, however long; a long tool call or simulation is never mistaken for a stall.
- `idle-done`: the turn ended with its output.
- `idle-stalled`: the session is idle but its step is not done, or the turn ended on an API error or an interrupt; detected in seconds from state, not from a timeout.
- `asking`: the agent waits on an answer.
- `dead`: the pane or process is gone.

Each state change is an event with a timestamp, so a consumer reacts to the change and keeps a history of changes only, never ticks (see `orch-notice-channel`).
`idle-stalled` gets a bounded resume: shuttle tells the session to continue, with a retry cap and backoff, then halts the run visibly with the cause.

## Sources, never guesses

Today's misreads all came from inference: scraping the pane (the idle probe, the paste race), scanning the transcript heuristically (missed `queued_command` lines, #411/#420), and judging from mtime or elapsed time (the 45 min quiet notice).
The model rests on what Claude Code itself reports:

- Hooks are the truth: `UserPromptSubmit` is a turn start, `Stop` a turn end (its payload carries `background_tasks`), `Notification` an agent asking or waiting on a permission. Shuttle already installs the Stop hook; the others are a few lines in the same hook config writing to the same event file. Hooks are only for agent sessions; lyx's own Go processes know their state already.
- An API error is a marked transcript entry; whether Claude Code also has a hook for it is to be checked.
- Liveness is the process: a dead pid is `dead`.
- The pane is a cross-check only, never the basis.
- Missing or contradicting signals give `unknown`, shown, never a silent guess.

Tests replay the real transcripts and hook payloads that today's and yesterday's failures left behind as fixtures.

## Built in small steps

A big-bang rewrite of shuttle is the risk; nothing changes behavior until it is proven:

1. `shuttle-turns` lands first.
2. Shadow mode: shuttle computes and logs the state beside today's guesses, with no consumer reading it; disagreements are read against real runs.
3. One consumer moves at a time, each its own small task: batten's quiet notice first (worst case a wrong notice), then the orch watcher, then creel.

## Relations

`shuttle-turns` fixes turn reading and is a first piece of this; this note is the step after it lands.
`run-recovery` covers dead processes; `orch-notice-channel` and `orch-compact-timeout` are consumers that would read this state; `creel` stage 2 delivers on it.


## A held turn end shows as a wait

From run-recovery PR-Gate (2026-10-07): run-recovery made every wait visible (reed `@lyx_wait` mark, `waits` token, `lyx loom status` waiting line) for verify, gate and background-shell waits. shuttle-turns adds a new hold state, a turn end without output that holds; unless it sets a wait mark too, a held session looks like a hang. Wire the hold into the same marker files once both have landed.
Also from shuttle-turns PR-Gate (2026-10-07): a gated run whose last event is a waiting turn end with every output file present can sit up to `background_shell_wait_min` (10 min) before it finishes Done.


## A stuck outcome is not a question

Seen 2026-10-07 in card-batching: the batten notice and loom status said `webster master is asking a question`, but the master had written `_lyx/webster/outcome.yaml` with `outcome: stuck` plus `summary.md` and ended its turn. The stop must be classified from the outcome file, not as a question; see `session-state` for the wider model.

## From issue #429

Imported from [issue #429](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/429).

**What happened**

During the Webster row, Master delegated a batch to a fork that ran a long after-state measurement in a background shell.
Master's turn ended with only interim fork output, because it was holding `record-batch` until the fork's final completion notification.
lyx's wait ran past `background_shell_wait_min` (10 minutes), stopped waiting and counted Master's turn end.
It did not stop the shell.
The run's outcome became `error: webster: master asked a question instead of finishing`, and the loom halted `blocked` with anomaly `escalation-to-human`.

Friction notes reported "Master's wait counted a turn end past a background shell" twice, in two different Master sessions.
The driver re-stepped the Webster row after a binary change (`last_step.binary_changed`) and Master blocked the same way a second time, still waiting on the same fork's measurement.
The halt recurred, so one re-step does not clear it.

**Why this is abnormal**

An interim "still waiting on a background job" turn end is not a question to a human, and halting the loom as `escalation-to-human` for it needs an operator for no reason.
The wait gives up on the shell after a fixed time, but the shell and the Master strand stay alive until the next `lyx webster run` reclaims them, so the work being waited on is killed or orphaned on the very re-step meant to recover.
The log line "stopping a leftover live strand before respawning it; an in-flight batch run restarts from state.json rather than resuming" shows the re-step discards the pending wait.

**What to do**

- Do not classify a Master turn end that is waiting on a live fork or background shell as a question or an `error`.
- Either keep waiting while the fork's background job is live, or resume Master when the job completes, instead of halting.
- If giving up after `background_shell_wait_min` stays, stop the shell and surface a distinct anomaly, not `escalation-to-human`.

Provenance: task `test-tiers`; notes `webster-background-shell.md`, `webster-background-shell-2.md`, `loom-halt.md`, `loom-halt-2.md`, `driver-restep-20261007-webster-blocked.md`.


## A deliberate permission setup

Operator 2026-10-03, while striking the roadmap's shuttle generic tools-restriction: restricting tools per agent is meaningless today, but lyx needs a correct setup of denied and allowed tools and commands, so nothing gets blocked.
Seen the same day: the global deny list (`git reset --hard`, removed by the operator; `git push --force` still in) stopped `pair-lifecycle` twice at steps lyx itself prescribed.
Related: `no-denied-recovery`, `orch-live-hardening` (permission modes mean what they say).

Seen 2026-10-04 in `board-model` (#361): Webster Master ran `python3 - …` with a misplaced heredoc, the shell hung on stdin and blocked the verify gate for 75 minutes.
Operator: lyx agents never use Python. Nothing denies it today: agents run in bypass, and shuttle's PreToolUse hook (`internal/shuttleengine/claudeengine/settings.go`) guards only other cases. Want: the same hook denies `python`/`python3` in Bash for every lyx-spawned agent, with a reason pointing to Edit/Write and grep/awk.

entries.title: reed: strand and run tabs, narrow-terminal run row, a color per strand role
entries.brief: VIEW plus a zoom button per strand and Alt-key navigation, run tabs that never fall off a narrow terminal, and each strand role in its own color
entries.body:
The run view in reed: strands as zoomable tabs, runs as session tabs that fit a narrow terminal, and a color per strand role.

## Strand and run tabs

reed runs one tmux session per run on the hub's one server, each with one window named `claude` whose panes are the run's strands, so the default status line shows nothing to switch between and a strand is hard to see on its own.

Chosen by the operator 2026-10-05 after a live demo on a separate server (`tmux -L lyxdemo`, session `run-c`): keep reed's current layout as the overview (driver on top at its fixed height, spawned strands below taking the rest, Selvage one line at the bottom), and show one strand at a time by zooming it.
Everything below is tmux's own options and bindings; reed pins them at server boot, like the `mouse` pin in `internal/reedengine/lifecycle.go`, so they survive a server restart.

- Line 1: a `VIEW` button lit when nothing is zoomed, then one button per strand, lit when that strand is zoomed; Selvage gets no button.
- Strand names come from a pane user option `@strand` that reed sets when it starts the strand (e.g. `driver`, `discussion-writer`), not from `pane_title`, which Claude Code overwrites with its own title; Selvage carries no `@strand`, which is what skips it.
- Line 2: one button per run (session), the current one lit, and the clock.
- Alt+z toggles between the overview and the zoomed strand; Alt+Up/Down moves to the previous/next strand and keeps the zoom; Alt+Left/Right switches run (operator, 2026-10-06).
- Pane borders carry the strand's title.

```
status 2
status-style bg=colour234,fg=white
status-format[0] "#[align=left]#{?window_zoomed_flag,#[bg=colour238#,fg=white],#[bg=cyan#,fg=black#,bold]} VIEW #[default]  #{P:#{?#{@strand},#[range=pane|#{pane_id}]#{?#{&&:#{window_zoomed_flag},#{pane_active}},#[bg=cyan#,fg=black#,bold],#[bg=colour236#,fg=white]} #{@strand} #[norange default] ,}}"
status-format[1] "#[align=left]#{S:#[range=session|#{session_id}]#{?#{==:#{session_name},#{client_session}},#[bg=yellow#,fg=black#,bold],#[bg=colour238#,fg=white]} #{session_name} #[norange default] }#[align=right]%H:%M "
pane-border-status top
pane-border-format " #{?pane_active,#[bold],}#{?#{@strand},#{@strand},selvage} "
bind -n M-z resize-pane -Z
bind -n M-Up select-pane -t :.- -Z
bind -n M-Down select-pane -t :.+ -Z
bind -n M-Left switch-client -p
bind -n M-Right switch-client -n
```

Status formats are one array: setting one index on a single session drops the global lines for that session, so set them globally only.

Open:

- Clicking a strand button while zoomed unzooms (tmux's default `MouseDown1Status` selects the pane); a root binding that re-zooms after the switch when the window was zoomed keeps it zoomed.
- Check that Claude Code does not need Alt+arrows or Alt+z in its input; tmux takes them first.
- VS Code's terminal swallows Alt+arrows and Alt+z, while Konsole passes them through; on 2026-10-06 the operator's user `keybindings.json` got one `workbench.action.terminal.sendSequence` entry per key (`\u001b[1;3A`–`D`, `\u001bz`, `when: terminalFocus`), which made them reach tmux.
  VS Code binds these keys itself (Alt+Left/Right focus the previous/next terminal in a group, Alt+z toggles word wrap), so the terminal never forwards them.
  `lyx ide` seeds these entries as part of its setup (operator, 2026-10-06); VS Code has no per-workspace keybindings, so they go in the user `keybindings.json` as a marked `// lyx:begin` … `// lyx:end` block that `lyx ide` rewrites, as mill does with its own block.
- `switch-client -n`/`-p` steps sessions in name order, but the `#{S:}` loop draws them in session-id order, so Alt+Left/Right jumped around the bar; on 2026-10-06 the bindings were replaced by a `run-shell` helper that steps through `list-sessions` sorted by session id.
  The operator wants spawn order (it matches how the runs sit on their desktop), so the bar keeps session-id order and switching follows it; the helper becomes a lyx verb such as `lyx reed switch --next|--prev` that the keys call.
  The binding passes `--socket '#{socket_path}' --client '#{client_name}'`, so the verb resolves nothing from a working directory: it lists the server's sessions, sorts them by session id and switches that client.
  Session ids are reassigned when the server restarts, so reed recreates the sessions in spawn order (the prime first, then each pair by its run's start time, read from the pair's own records), which keeps the order across a restart.
- Alt+Up/Down cycles every pane, Selvage included; skip it, e.g. by binding to a short reed-free tmux command that steps over panes without `@strand`.

Rejected in the demo: one window per strand (loses the overview, since a pane lives in one window only) and grouped sessions for a second view (hard to attach).

Related: `strand-colors` could tint the strand buttons and borders per role.


## Run tabs on a narrow terminal

## Seen 2026-10-06

With five runs and the prime open, the session row of the status line (the run tabs from `reed-status-tabs`) is wider than a narrow terminal, and the rightmost runs fall off the edge with no sign that they exist.
The row prints every session's full name with padding, and run slugs such as `test-suite-prune-core` are long.

## Options

1. Current session full, others truncated, overflow scrolls (recommended): the session the client is in shows its full name, every other session is cut to about 12 characters (`#{=12:session_name}`), and the row uses tmux's list mode (`list=on`, `list=focus`, left and right markers), so a row that still overflows scrolls with `<` and `>` markers and keeps the current session visible.
2. Index only for other sessions, the current one by full name: the most compact, but the operator has to remember which number is which run.
3. List-mode scrolling alone, full names kept: the least change, with the fewest sessions visible at once.
4. Wrap the session row onto further status lines: costs terminal height, and tmux has no automatic wrap, so reed would compute the split itself.

The run tabs' design is in the note `reed-status-tabs`.


## A color per strand role

## Problem

With a run live, the driver pane and the agents it spawns (Webster, Burler, Bouncer judge, Describe and the rest) look alike in tmux and in Claude Code, so it is often hard to see which session is which.

## Idea (operator, 2026-10-05)

Give each spawned session a color with Claude Code's `/color` command, so the driver stands apart from the agents it spawns.
Open question: one color per loom segment (Discussion, Plan, Webster, review, Describe, landing) rather than only driver against the rest; the operator would like that.

## Open

- Where the color is set: by the spawning code through reed when it starts the strand, or by the agent's own launch prompt.
- Whether the tmux pane border or the strand tabs of `reed-status-tabs` should carry the same color, so the reed layout matches the sessions.

entries.title: Shuttle: a Send lands or retries, and attach knows a half it stopped
entries.brief: Send waits for a ready pane and a settled input before Enter, retries with backoff, and a lost submission is transient; attach no longer halts on a stopped Burler half
entries.body:
A text shuttle sends into an agent pane lands, and when it cannot, the run retries instead of halting.

Seen 2026-10-08 in `plan-glyph-precision`, under high machine load: the skill-load `Send` into a freshly started Burler half left the text pending in Claude Code's input box after 2 extra Enters, the step failed as `producer-hard-failure`, and the driver had to re-step by hand; the re-step then halted on a run dir it could not classify.

## From issue #442

## What happened

A loom run halted `failed` (anomaly `producer-hard-failure`) at the `Discussion-Burler` row, round 2 attempt 2.
The error chain:

```
shedadapters: Discussion-Burler (burler): round 2 attempt 2: run: burler: shuttle run: shuttle: load skills [scribe:prose scribe:code-quality scribe:testing]: shuttle: Send: the sent text is still pending in the input box after 2 extra Enter(s); the submission did not land
```

Earlier rows in the same run (`Discussion-Write`, and the first `Discussion-Burler` attempt) completed; this was the first submission failure.

## Why it is abnormal

The shuttle's skill-load `Send` types the text into the agent's tmux pane, presses Enter, and gives up after 2 extra Enters when the text is still in the input box.
A transient pane state (agent busy, input not yet ready, paste not yet consumed) turns into a hard producer failure that halts the whole run.
Nothing in the failure distinguishes "agent not ready to accept input" from "submission lost", and no retry or wait-for-idle precedes the give-up.

## What to do

- Before giving up in `Send`, wait for the pane to be ready for input, then retry the submission with backoff rather than a fixed 2 extra Enters.
- Treat a failed skill-load submission as a retryable step (re-send once, or restart the shuttle attempt) instead of `producer-hard-failure`.
- Record the pane's last lines in the halt note so the cause (busy agent, modal prompt, unconsumed paste) is visible.

Provenance: task `plan-glyph-precision`, from `loom-halt.md`.



## From issue #443

**What happened**
During a loom run, the Discussion-Burler step (burler round 2, attempt 2) failed with a non-transient `producer` error from `shuttle: Send`:
`the sent text is still pending in the input box after 2 extra Enter(s); the submission did not land`.
The step was refused (`shed: step refused kind=producer`), so the skill load into the freshly started half never happened.
The trace had just logged `burler: stopping a live half of a round` before the refusal.
The only `fabric: mutation` records were a records commit and its push, so no half-finished add/remove was left behind.

**Why it is abnormal**
A Send into a live agent pane should either submit or fail with a retryable condition.
Giving up after 2 extra Enters turns a timing/pane-readiness problem into a hard, non-transient producer failure that halts the run as `failed`.

**What to do**
Make `shuttle: Send` verify pane readiness before sending (or retry with backoff and re-check the input box) and classify the pending-input outcome as transient so the shed retries the step instead of halting.
The driver recovered by re-stepping (`interrupt_policy: reinvoke`).

Provenance: task `plan-glyph-precision`; notes: `driver-repair-20261008-discussion-burler-1.md`.



## From issue #444

**What happened**
Re-stepping Discussion-Burler after the Send failure (see the companion issue on `shuttle: Send` leaving text pending) halted the run as `failed` with anomaly `producer-hard-failure`:
`round 2: probe the round's halves: burler: probe the burler-review half: shuttle: attach: 1 candidate run dir(s) under .lyx/shuttle cannot be confirmed dead or alive (untracked or with a cleared pane binding, younger than 3m0s): .lyx/shuttle/<run-id> — check "lyx reed status" and either wait or clear the stale directory by hand`.
The run history at the halt had 6 entries (Discussion-Bouncer/Burler alternating `stuck`).

**Why it is abnormal**
The candidate run dir is almost certainly the half that `burler: stopping a live half of a round` had just stopped in the previous attempt.
lyx created that state itself, yet the next probe cannot classify it and treats it as a hard failure instead of waiting out the 3m window.
An automated run should not need a manual "wait or clear by hand".

**What to do**
Have the stop path mark the run dir dead (or clear its pane binding explicitly) so the probe sees it as dead.
Alternatively make the probe's "cannot be confirmed" outcome transient, so the shed retries after the grace window rather than halting.

Provenance: task `plan-glyph-precision`; notes: `loom-halt.md`, `driver-repair-20261008-discussion-burler-1.md`.



## Direction

- Find the root cause in `Send` first: when it types, how it detects pending input, and when it presses Enter (paste not yet consumed, a session still starting, a readiness probe passing too early).
- Wait for the pane to be ready before typing and for the typed text to settle before Enter; retry Enter with backoff within a bounded time, re-reading the input box.
- A submission that still does not land is a transient error, so the step retries; the error carries the pane's last lines.
- `shuttle attach` tells a half that lyx itself just stopped from an unknown live run, so a re-step never halts on it.


## No send into a running turn after a restart

From `parent-review-hardening` (PR #336 review, 2026-10-02): `AttachGated` replays events from offset 0, so the first tick treats the writer as idle even mid-turn: a notify-carried prompt or a reject re-prompt can be typed into a running turn, and a consumed reject is let through while the writer is still fixing.
A send waits until the session is idle in fact, not by a replayed reading.

entries.title: Webster: recovery never dead-ends, stale config fails at the start, a computed Merriam base
entries.brief: Reset targets as lyx verbs, a recovery prompt that names a dirty tree, decisions that reach a begun card, a retryable failed record-batch, batcher.yaml checked in preflight, and a computed batchifier base
entries.body:
## Goal

Webster's recovery paths never dead-end: every recovery instruction names a lyx verb, a recovery prompt states the worktree it starts from, an operator decision reaches a begun card, a failed record-batch leaves a retryable batch, and a stale batcher config fails at the start of a run instead of mid-Webster.
The batchifier's Merriam base is computed instead of fitted.

## Reset targets

`webster-audit-recovery` (PR #381) added `lyx webster reset --to start|pre-fix` so recovery never needs a denied `git reset --hard`.
Three sites still tell the agent to run `git reset --keep <sha>` rather than a lyx verb.
They move back to the report head or the last-batch head in record-batch, recover-batch and accept-audit (`internal/websterengine/gitwrap.go`), plus standalone mode.

Widen `lyx webster reset` with the report-head and last-batch-head targets, and point the three sites and standalone mode at it, so every Webster recovery instruction names a lyx verb.

## Recovery prompt on a dirty tree (from issue #406)

A recovery run for a Webster segment was started with the reason `none` and an instruction to continue from the committed tree, while the worktree held a large uncommitted body of work from the earlier attempt.
The recovery prompt did not mention these changes or say whether to keep or discard them, so the agent had to judge on its own.

When lyx starts a recovery, it detects uncommitted changes in the worktree and names them in the recovery prompt, with an explicit keep-or-discard instruction.

Provenance: task `test-suite-prune-core`.

## An operator decision amends a begun card (from issue #413)

An operator decision made while Webster runs cannot reach the plan card of a batch that has begun.
Seen 2026-10-07 in `bugfix-sessions`: the decision went into the decision record, but `lyx webster rebaseline --card 01` refused ("the edited plan changes the cards of a batch this run already begun"), and its way forward, `lyx webster reset --to start` then `lyx webster run --fresh`, has no path through loom: the Webster producer always runs with `Fresh: false` (`internal/shedadapters/webster.go`).
An edit left on disk while the master recorded the batch blocked the run with `plan_drifted` until the plan was restored.

Issue #413 shows the same dead end from loom's own flow: a `goto` back to `Plan-Write` after batch 1 had begun re-ran Plan and Batchifier with an edited plan, `record-batch 1` refused with `plan_drifted` and named `rebaseline`, and `rebaseline` refused because the card had begun.
The first refusal's advice leads straight into the second, and the only exits discard the run's Webster progress.

Wanted (operator, 2026-10-07): an operator decision taken mid-Webster lands in the plan and the decision record together, without extra review or PR-Gate steps, whether or not the card's batch has begun.

Since `bugfix-webster` (d536a1a4e) the drift advice offers rebaseline only for an edit that keeps begun batches' cards, and rebaseline accepts an edit to a failed, dead or stuck batch.
Still open: a decision against a begun, non-terminal batch, a plan re-run by loom after a batch began, and the Webster producer's `Fresh: false`.

## begin-batch after a failed record-batch (from issue #441)

After `lyx webster record-batch` failed on a config-load error, `lyx webster begin-batch 1` refused: the batch already has a report and state.json records it as begun and not terminal.
A record-batch refusal that is not about the report itself leaves the batch begun with a report on disk, so the retry path through begin-batch is blocked, and the refusal lists several remedies without saying which applies.

- record-batch fails before touching batch state when its config does not load, or a re-run of record-batch after the config is fixed recovers the state.
- The begin-batch refusal names the remedy that applies to the recorded state.

Provenance: task `lifecycle-waits`.

## Stale batcher config caught at the start (from issue #440)

A run halted `blocked` at Webster when `record-batch` refused because the pair's `batcher.yaml` still carried `startup_context`, which the binary no longer accepts.
The run had passed Preflight, Loom-Preflight, Discussion, Plan and Batchifier before the drift surfaced, and it landed as a human escalation rather than a config failure.

- Preflight or Loom-Preflight loads and validates `batcher.yaml`, so schema drift fails at the start of a run.
- A removed key such as `startup_context` is migrated or reported clearly when a pair config was seeded from an older template.

Provenance: task `lifecycle-waits`.

## Computed Merriam base

Left from `batcher-v2`'s PR-Gate (2026-10-07).
`batcher-v2` sizes a batch's start context as `master_base + (k−1) × batch_growth`, with `master_base: 52000` a fitted constant in `internal/batcher/template.yaml`.
The operator wanted the base computed, since it is fixed by what Merriam loads.
Measured over three `cautious` runs, Merriam starts at about 20.6K and orients itself up to 50–54K before the first fork; a larger plan or another repo can land far from 52K.

- A function in `websterengine` computes Merriam's fixed part at partition time: CLAUDE.md, the Webster stencil with the inlined PATTERN overview, and the plan files Merriam reads; the system prompt and tools enter as a measured constant.
- `Batch` takes that value, beside `before`, and `startContext` becomes `computedBase + orientation + (k−1) × batch_growth`.
- `master_base` gives way to an `orientation` coefficient in `Weights`, `template.yaml` and the calibrate fit in `tools/tokencount`.

entries.title: lyx cleanup: one command runs every module cleanup
entries.brief: Drop finished batten statuses, prune the board, clear disposable .scratch and .lyx files, each through the owning module verb
entries.body:
## Wanted

The operator (2026-10-08): one command that tidies the repo, running every cleanup there is.
Today finished batten runs leave `_lyx/shed/<slug>/` behind in the records repo for good (one directory per slug that ever ran), done board entries wait for `lyx board prune`, and `.scratch/` and `.lyx/` gather drafts and logs nobody reads again.

## Proposal

- A top-level verb, such as `lyx cleanup`, that only calls each module's own cleanup verb, so no module learns about another's state.
- Batten's cleanup removes the status directory of every run whose status is terminal and done; it never touches a running, halted or failed run.
- It runs `lyx board prune`.
- It clears what `.scratch/` and `.lyx/` hold that can be discarded: old orch notes beyond the latest, logs past an age, stale drafts.
  Which `.lyx/` paths are disposable is a design call for the task that builds it.
- A dry run lists what would go before anything is removed.

Related: note `batten-reused-slug`, where a leftover done status blocked a new task with the same slug.

entries.title: Audit how plans use glyphs in practice, then tune the plan stencil
entries.brief: Runs only after many tasks have landed with glyph plans: measure glyph use, how writers find glyphs, Plan rounds and handle binding from real runs; kick-start waits on it
entries.body:
## Why

`plan-glyph-precision` makes plan cards name the members they change as glyphs, gated by the plan validators, and its committed test proves the glyph chain over a fixture module.
That proves the machinery, not that plan writers use it well.
The operator (2026-10-08) doubts a writer can pick the right glyphs from its own reasoning, and expects the gate to cost Plan rounds and time.
Kick-start packs (`kick-start-pack`, `enclose-kickstart`) build on plans whose glyphs resolve, so they wait until practice shows that.

## Proposal

Audit the first runs after `plan-glyph-precision` lands from their logs and transcripts:

- the share of `Edit:` targets that are member glyphs rather than file paths or self glyphs;
- the Plan rounds and Plan wall time spent on glyph findings (unresolved glyphs, redundancy, caller coverage, the re-sign arrow), against the Plan time of earlier runs;
- `plan:` handles declared, bound at record-batch, and failed;
- members a card edited that its glyphs did not name, and glyphs that named the wrong member, read from the batch diffs;
- how the plan writer arrives at each glyph, read from the Plan-Write transcript: the `lyx quarry` calls it made, the greps and file reads around them, and how many tries a glyph took before it resolved (operator, 2026-10-08: the search may be mostly trial and error, and its cost belongs in the audit);
- test-file paths under `Edit:`: the plan template (`loom-template-plan.md`) allows a plain path for "a test file the card adds tests to", and the rubric flags only non-test Go paths, so every test file goes in as a path (operator, 2026-10-08); count from the batch diffs how many of those paths changed existing members (a test, a fake such as `fakes_test.go`, a helper) that a glyph could have named, and whether new tests could be declared as `plan:` handles like new production members;
- whether implementer and Burler forks use the card's glyphs at execution time (a `lyx quarry` lookup) or fall back to grep and whole-file reads.

## First data points (2026-10-08)

- `shuttle-send`: 93 of 139 `Edit:`/`Create:` targets are glyphs; every plain path is a test, `doc.go`, `template.yaml` or markdown file; one self-check round of 10 `glyph-not-found` (plan-created members named without `plan:`), fixed in one pass; Plan-Write about 13 minutes, Plan-Review one round.
- `review-lens-fan`: 34 of 50 targets are glyphs, again with no plain path to non-test Go source.

The plan stencil already tells writers to copy glyphs from `lyx quarry` answers and never spell one; plans before this task still named mostly file paths, because a path was always a valid target.
The audit's main question is whether the share of plain paths falls once `plan-glyph-precision`'s member-glyph rules and rubric flag are in place.
From what it shows, tune the plan stencil and rubric where writers still fall back to paths or take many gate rounds.
Kick-start work starts only once the audit shows plans name resolvable members in practice.

entries.title: Review loop: a lighter convergence rule, a three-round default budget, models per segment
entries.brief: Converge without circling to the budget on fresh edge-case keys, default the round budget to 3, set review and fix models per segment, an option to start the fixer after the review, and circling decisions that resume the run
entries.body:
## What happened

On 2026-10-08 the Discussion review segments of `plan-glyph-precision`, `shuttle-state` and `reed-view` all ran their five rounds and escalated to the parent with cause `budget`.
In each, the round-5 reviewer's verdict was APPROVED with no BLOCKING finding, every earlier key was resolved, and each round raised fresh keys on edge cases rather than repeating old ones.
The parent then recorded the remaining design calls as decisions and accepted, which another round would not have changed.

The judge's decision rule (`decisionRuleMarker` in `internal/shedadapters/bouncerprompt.go`) says `CONTINUE` while the latest round carries any `design` finding at MEDIUM or worse, and the judge stencil counts no fix as convergence, because a fix is new text no fresh reviewer has seen.
Every round's fixes so yield a fresh full review and fresh MEDIUM keys until the budget runs out; the reviewer's own verdict carries no weight.

Measured over the ten latest landed runs (2026-10-08), review loops take about 57% of a run's agent time (median about 24 min Discussion, 27 min Plan, 34 min Webster review, against 39 min of Webster execution), with median rounds 3.5, 2.5 and 2.5, and 5 of 10 Discussion reviews escalated on budget.
Nearly all of a round is the reviewer pass; the judge takes under a minute.

## Proposal

- **A lighter convergence rule:** `CONVERGED` when the latest round carries no BLOCKING finding and no MEDIUM `design` finding on a key that was already open in an earlier round.
  New MEDIUM keys in the closing round are not dropped: they go to the next producer through the decision record, as the parent did by hand on 2026-10-08.
  BLOCKING always continues.
- **A default budget of three rounds (operator, 2026-10-08):** the template default of `review_max_bounces` (`internal/loomengine/template.yaml`) drops from 5 to 3; a spent budget still escalates to the parent, who decides what to do ("it is mostly fine after three rounds").
  The prime's own `loom.yaml` already carries 3.
- **Models per segment:** `loom.yaml`'s `review` and `fix` keys take one model-spec or a per-round list, but one setting serves every review segment.
  The task lets each segment (Discussion, Plan, Webster review) set its own review and fix models, with today's keys as the default.
- **An option to start the fixer when the review is done:** the fixer starts beside the reviewer and polls `lyx burler await-review` so its orientation overlaps the review (572ab84e8).
  When a review runs longer than the prompt-cache TTL the fixer's cache expires while it waits, and each await poll is a paid turn.
  The task adds a config option to start the fixer only once the review file exists instead; today's parallel start stays the default (operator, 2026-10-08: only the option for now).

The lens fan for Discussion and Plan is task `review-lens-fan`, which waits on `shuttle-state`.

## Circling decisions resume the run (from issue #446)

Imported from [issue #446](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/446).

After `lyx loom circling accept plan-glyph-precision` (Discussion-Bouncer round 5, cause budget, under a watching batten run), the verb printed `"resume":"lyx loom start"`, and `lyx loom resume` in the task worktree then refused: "the run is awaiting a decision, which resume does not give; run \"lyx loom approve\" or \"lyx loom reject\"", although the decision was recorded and approve/reject are PR-Gate verbs.
The run moved on only after the driver stepped it.

Expected: after `circling accept` or `continue` under a watching batten run, both outputs name the same next step, and `loom resume` either resumes on the recorded circling decision or says the decision is recorded and the driver will step it.
The hub's role tells it to run `lyx loom resume` after a circling decision.

entries.title: Review lens fans for Discussion and Plan, narrowed by the judge each round
entries.brief: Wire burler cluster review into Discussion and Plan with their own fans, let the judge drop settled lenses, after shuttle-state settles gate quiescence with forks
entries.body:
## Why

Discussion and Plan review run solo: one reviewer per round, no lenses.
Burler's fork-based cluster review (`df1c6ba33`: the lens and fan library in `burler.yaml`, the judge's `exclude_lenses` channel) has never been wired into `loom-recipe.yaml`; no review row sets `cluster-fan`.
The cluster design is what lets a review cover a subject broadly in one round; a solo reviewer covers one slice per round, so fresh edge cases surface round after round.
Review loops are the largest share of a run's agent time (see task `review-loop-convergence`).

## Proposal

- Turn on a cluster fan for the Discussion and Plan review rows (`cluster-fan` on the BurlerRound rows, `cluster_excludes: true` on their Bouncer rows, which `internal/loomrecipe/clusterexcludes_test.go` pins to agree).
  Webster review stays solo: its forks may run no git and cannot reach a diff-only subject (the recipe comment on that row).
- Discussion and Plan get their own fans in `burler.yaml`, with lenses written for a design record and a plan rather than the code-oriented `standard` lenses (error-handling, test-gaps).
- Round 1 runs the broad fan; the judge narrows it each bounce through `exclude_lenses`, dropping lenses whose area is settled, so later rounds cost less.

## Blocker: gate quiescence with forks

A hub quick fix adding the fan stopped at `TestNoGatedRowAuthorizesForkSubagents` (`internal/loomrecipe/gatequiescence_test.go`), which pins a deliberately declined decision: a gated run must not spawn forks, because a gate fires at turn end and turn-idle alone would no longer mean the agent is finished.
Since the reviewer/fixer split (572ab84e8) the recipe's `gates` reach only the fixer, which never forks, but the reviewer, the half that forks under a fan, carries its own review-parse gate (`ReviewGateEntry`), so the question stands for any fan.
`shuttle-state` makes a turn end with outstanding background work the Stop payload reports a wait rather than a finished turn (its D8); this task re-opens the declined decision on that ground, rewrites or narrows the test, and corrects Webster-Burler's "Single reviewer, matching both shipped segments" comment.

## Cost and time

`docs/research/session-fork-spike.md` measured Claude Code fork subagents with a full prefix cache hit: about 17K fresh compute per extra reviewer after one shared explore phase, against about 209K for a cold reviewer.
So a fan's extra lenses are cheap next to the explore phase, which is paid once per round.
The forks run in parallel, so a round takes about the explore phase plus the slowest lens plus consolidation; the spike measured no wall-clock time.
The task measures tokens and wall time per round and per segment against solo rounds before the fan becomes the default.

## Models

Operator, 2026-10-08: a fanned review's forks run on sonnet, while a solo reviewer runs on opus; code review (Webster-Review) runs on sonnet either way.
The fan's fork model is its own setting, separate from the segment's solo `review` model.

entries.title: Capture real hook payloads into fixtures

`shuttle-state` added recording hooks for `UserPromptSubmit`, `StopFailure`, `Notification` and `SessionEnd`, with an `llm`-tier capture scenario that was compiled but never run.

entries.title: Shuttle: the launch line carries the first turn
entries.brief: /color already goes through the verified send; the skill-load message or the prompt should ride the launch line so only later turns are typed
entries.body:
## Why

Shuttle types `/color <color>` into a fresh session's pane, and with skills it types the skill-load message and then the prompt as well.
Every typed send is a chance for a lost or half-landed message, and the operator finds the typing clumsy (2026-10-08).

## Facts (Claude Code 2.1.294 CLI reference)

- No CLI flag, settings key or environment variable sets the session color; `/color` in the session is the only way.
- The positional `claude "<text>"` submits its text as the first user turn of an interactive session, and a slash command or skill invocation works there.
- Only one positional prompt exists, so the launch line carries one first turn.

## Proposal

- The launch line carries the first turn in every case: the skill-load message when skills are named, else the prompt, so only the turns after the first are typed.
- `/color` stays typed, as there is no launch-time alternative, but goes through shuttle's verified send once `shuttle-send` lands, after the session is ready.

## Priority

Operator, 2026-10-08: low; the typed skill load is robust, and the launch line saves only a little time.

## Done on 2026-10-08

`/color` goes through shuttle's verified send after the session is ready (main e12fb6afb, with the settle wait from 7b3d140cb).
What remains is the first proposal bullet: the launch line carries the first turn.

entries.title: lyx pause: stop every run at once, safely and on purpose
entries.brief: A hub-wide pause that interrupts every Claude session with Esc within seconds, unlike the step-boundary pauses, recorded as ordered so no failure or idle path fires
entries.body:
## Why

The operator suspends the laptop while runs are in flight.
A sleep can cut a network call or an agent turn midway (a weft push hung a batten run for 2.5 hours after a hibernate, #458), and after resume idle notices fire for time that was only sleep.

The existing `lyx batten pause` and `lyx loom pause` only set a request the machine consumes at its next producer boundary: they kill nothing, so an agent turn, a Webster batch or a review round runs on until it ends, which can be an hour.
That is not enough to make the hub safe to suspend.

## Proposal (operator, 2026-10-08)

- One hub-wide verb, named `lyx pause` (the operator's choice of name), that safely stops every lyx process within a short time.
- It gives running work a few seconds to finish cleanly, such as a bash command completing.
- It interrupts every running Claude Code instance by sending Esc.
- A pause is ordered and intentional: it must not trigger the paths for an unexpected stop, such as batten notices, the agents-idle or driver-dead conditions, review-round failures or crash recovery.
- The step-boundary pause is not good enough and goes: it is how Millhouse had to pause, and lyx now has the means to interrupt agents directly (shuttle's session state from hooks, the reed panes, shuttle's stop verb).

## Open design points

- Resuming: whether a matching verb resumes every paused run where it stood, and how each role takes up its interrupted turn (loom's `interrupt_policy` already distinguishes `reinvoke` from `handback`).
- Scope: whether the orch session is paused too, or only runs.
- Per-run use: whether `lyx pause <slug>` pauses one run the same way, now that the boundary pause goes.
- Relation to shuttle's stop verb from `shuttle-send`, which settles a run's record before removing its strand.

entries.title: reed: strands state their size; parallel agents share the window evenly
entries.brief: Replace the one collapse-all-but-the-newest rule with per-strand sizing: content-sized panes like the runs overview, and parallel agents that share space evenly
entries.body:
## Why

reed has one layout rule (`internal/reedengine/doc.go`, "The layout rule"): the strands stack in insertion order, every strand but the bottom-most takes `collapsed_rows` rows, and the bottom-most takes every remaining row.
It fits a run whose newest agent is the one that matters, and nothing else:

- `runs-overview` wants a small pane under the orch, sized to its content, with the orch above keeping the space; today the orch would collapse to `collapsed_rows` and the overview would grow.
- `multi-agent-producer` runs N agents in parallel, none more important than the others; each needs a large share of the window, and none may collapse.

## Proposal (operator, 2026-10-08)

- A strand states how it is sized instead of taking its size from its position.
- At least two kinds: a fixed or content-sized strand (the overview: as few rows as show all its lines), and a sharing strand that splits the remaining space evenly with the other sharing strands.
- The agents of one multi-agent step share the window evenly, side by side or stacked; which of the two is open.
- The collapsed stack of finished agents may stay as one kind among these, for strands kept only for reference.

## Columns (operator, 2026-10-08)

The layout rules need a broader revision: tmux under reed can show any arrangement, so stacking strands side by side in columns, rather than in rows, is tempting as the main rule.

## Open

- Side by side (columns) or stacked rows for parallel agents, or a rule by window width.
- Who sets a strand's kind: the spawning producer through its seat table (`multi-agent-producer`), or reed by role.
- How `runs-overview`'s content-sized pane learns its height as runs come and go, and whether reed re-applies the layout on each change.

entries.title: A hub survives a lyx binary change; the no-script rule reaches spawned agents
entries.brief: Config reconciles itself on the first lyx command after a binary change, stencil drift behind main stops warning source-ahead, and file-editing stencils state the no-script edit rule
entries.body:
## Goal

A hub keeps working across a `lyx` binary change, and every rule a file-editing agent must follow reaches it.

## Part 1: config reconciles itself after a binary change

### Why

From webster-dead-ends PR-Gate (2026-10-08): that task retired the batcher keys `master_base` and `startup_context`, and Loom-Preflight now refuses a `batcher.yaml` that still carries them, pointing to `lyx config reconcile --apply`.
After the deploy the hub ran a manual reconcile in the prime and in every in-flight pair.

### Proposal (operator, 2026-10-08)

The trigger is a changed `lyx` binary, not a deploy: `update-plugins.sh` is loomyard's own route, and every other repo only gets a new binary.

- Each hub keeps a stamp under its `.lyx` naming the binary that last reconciled its config.
- The first `lyx` command in the hub that runs under a different binary reconciles the prime and every pair of the hub once, logs what it migrated, and writes the stamp.
- It runs before the command itself, so the orch, `lyx orch start` and `lyx batten run` already work with the new config; it cannot wait for the recipe's `Preflight` row, since the orch runs outside any recipe.
- The recipe's `Preflight` row checks the same stamp as a safety net and runs the reconcile when it is stale.
- A reconcile that cannot apply (a hand-edited conflict) stops the command with the reconcile's own way forward rather than running on a stale config.

### Open

- Concurrency: two `lyx` commands starting at once after a binary change; the reconcile takes a hub lock.
- Whether the same stamp also covers `stencil-drift-behind-main`: a pair behind the new binary is expected after a binary change, not a source-ahead fault.

### Also from that PR-Gate

`merriamFixedContext` is a constant from one measurement, so the system-prompt-and-tools figure drifts silently as Claude Code changes; a calibrate step in `tools/tokencount` could re-measure it.

## Part 2: stencil drift behind main is not source-ahead

Imported from [issue #445](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/445).

Seen: `lyx loom status` in each of three task pairs (plan-glyph-precision, shuttle-state, reed-view) logs
`stencilstore: board copy has drifted from worktree source; the board copy is untouched and a binary older than the source deployed it -- run a production deploy (update-plugins.sh)` with `stencil=webster-template-master class=source-ahead`.

The pairs branched from main at fd5b0f58e; main and prod then moved to c0bf19c54, which changed `contracts/stencils/webster/webster-template-master.md`.
The installed binary is c0bf19c54 and the board copy matches c0bf19c54, so the pair's source is behind the board copy, not ahead, and a deploy fixes nothing.
The prime logs no warning.

Expected: a worktree whose source is older than the board copy (a pair that branched before the last deploy) is not classified source-ahead and does not ask for a production deploy; at most it notes that the pair is behind main.

Workaround: none needed; the warning is ignored until the pairs sync with main at Finalize.

## Part 3: the no-script edit rule reaches spawned agents

Seen 2026-10-06 in `test-suite-prune-core`, batch 10's recovery strand: the agent edited `internal/websterengine/beginbatch_test.go` with an inline `python3 - <<'EOF'` script, and the edit left an unused `strconv` import that vet caught.

The rule "change files only with Edit or Write, never with a script that rewrites them (sed, awk, perl, python, node)" lives in `scribe:conversation`, a chat skill.
Spawned implementer, recovery and fixer roles load `scribe:prose`, `scribe:code-quality` and `scribe:testing`, so they never see it.

Fix direction: state the rule where every file-editing role reads it: the implementer and recovery stencils under `contracts/stencils/webster/`, the Burler fixer and Rework stencils, or one shared prefix they all compose.
