entries.title: Plan gate checks: precise callers, nested fixture modules, a reviewer that knows the gate
entries.brief: Resolve callers by import path and receiver type, let gates run against nested fixture modules, and give the plan reviewer the gate check list
entries.body:
## Goal

The plan gate's checks in planparser and quarry give no false findings: callers resolve by import path and receiver type, gates can run against nested fixture modules, and the plan reviewer sees the gate's checks so it proposes no fix the gate blocks.

## From `caller-uncovered-false-positives`

Imported from [issue #461](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/461).

**What happened:** Adding re-sign arrows to a plan card made the `caller-uncovered` check emit 75 informational entries, all false positives.
Every file that names a type counted as a caller of a re-signed method on a different type that happens to share the name, and any `.start(` call anywhere counted as a caller of a re-signed `start` method on one specific type.
The real callers had to be separated out by grep.

**Why it is abnormal:** The matching is by name only, not by receiver type, so the noise can hide a real uncovered caller.

**What to do:** Resolve callers by receiver type (or at least qualify the match by package and receiver) in `caller-uncovered`, and rate-limit or collapse name-only matches.

Provenance: task `webster-dead-ends`, note `burler-plan-r4.md`.


## From `caller-scan-import-path`

`plan-glyph-precision` added the `caller-uncovered` plan-gate check (D5).
Its caller scan matches by package clause name, so it cannot see a caller that imports the package under an alias or a dot import, nor a caller in a file an earlier card creates.
Both are accepted bounds in that task's decision record.
Resolving imports by path would close the first gap; worth building only if planners hit it.

### Seen in webster-dead-ends, 2026-10-08

Its plan gate reported 75 informational `caller-uncovered` entries on one card, all false positives by the fixer's grep:
every file naming the `batcher.Batch` interface type was read as a caller of the re-signed concrete method `costBatcher.Batch`,
and unrelated `.start(` calls as callers of `peakAccumulator.start`, matched by method name alone.
For a method the finding is informational, so it cost no round, but the noise hides a real uncovered caller.
Resolving a method call's receiver type would remove both classes.


## From `plan-gate-nested-module`

Imported from [issue #451](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/451).

### What happened

Two cards in one task had gates running `go test -tags integration` on package paths under a `testdata/` fixture directory.
The same card (or an earlier one) creates a `go.mod` in that directory, which makes the fixture its own module.
The main module then no longer contains those packages, so `go test` reports `main module does not contain package ... [setup failed]` and the gate's `&&` chain cannot pass as written.
The implementing agent worked around it by running `go vet` and `go test -tags integration ./...` from inside the fixture module, and wrote a friction note each time.

A related symptom in the same batch: the test-budget guard (`cmd/lyx/testdata/test-budget.yaml`) needed a package row raised on several cards, and that file was on no card's target list.

### Why it is abnormal

The plan was accepted through the plan gate although its gates were unsatisfiable by construction.
Plan validation does not check that a gate's package paths stay inside the module that the plan's own cards create or change.
Cards also do not predict the test-budget row they will cross, so each agent edits an untargeted file.

### What to do

- At plan-write or plan-review time, flag a gate command whose package path lies under a directory that a card makes a nested module (a `go.mod` in a card target), and require the gate to run inside that module.
- Consider listing `cmd/lyx/testdata/test-budget.yaml` as an implicit target, or surfacing the budget row in the card template, when a card adds tests.

Provenance: task `plan-glyph-precision`; notes `01-glyphchain-plan-gate.md`, `07-redundant-package-target.md`.


## From `plan-review-redundant-pairing`

Imported from [issue #460](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/460).

**What happened:** A plan-review fix said to keep a file target beside a member target of that file on the same card, on the premise that a file and a member of it on the same card do not overlap.
The plan gate's `redundant-file-target` check blocks exactly that pairing, so applying the fix as written failed validation, and both cards had to drop the file target again.

**Why it is abnormal:** The reviewer proposes a fix the gate rejects, which costs a wasted fix round.
A reviewer with the gate's check list in view would not suggest it.

**What to do:** Give the plan reviewer the gate's check list (at least `redundant-file-target`), or have its fixes validated against the gate before they are handed to the fixing agent.

Provenance: task `webster-dead-ends`, note `burler-plan-r4.md`.

entries.title: Webster record-batch and rebaseline: no needless re-drive, a calibrated Merriam base
entries.brief: Accept a prefix head_sha, find forked batch transcripts, accept a Card-Index-only change on an older record, and re-measure the Merriam fixed context
entries.body:
## Goal

Webster's record-batch and rebaseline in websterengine never force a needless re-drive or dead end: an abbreviated head_sha that prefixes HEAD is accepted, a forked batch's transcripts are found, a Card-Index-only change is accepted on a record without an overview frame, and the Merriam fixed context can be re-measured. The first half of plan-gate-done-cards (the plan gate skips done cards) landed on main on 2026-10-08; only its rebaseline half is in scope.

## From `record-batch-short-sha`

Imported from [issue #456](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/456).

`lyx webster record-batch` refused a batch report because the report's `head_sha` was an abbreviated SHA (9 characters) while the worktree's HEAD is the full 40-character SHA.

Refusal text (paths trimmed):

```
webster: batch report _lyx/webster/reports/01-carry-over-write.yaml: head_sha "ae24b9bb0" does not match the worktree's actual HEAD "ae24b9bb0eca5384fc9fd38764b9cb446aced655"; only merge commits, such as a parent merge-in, may sit between a fork's reported head and HEAD; way forward: 1) run `git reset --keep ae24b9bb0` to move HEAD back to the report's head_sha; 2) re-run this verb
```

Why this is abnormal: the abbreviated SHA is a prefix of HEAD, so the report names the right commit.
The comparison looks like an exact string match, so it reports a mismatch and then suggests `git reset --keep` to the commit HEAD already is, which is a no-op and does not resolve the refusal.
A fork writing `git rev-parse --short HEAD` into the report is a natural thing to do.

What to do: resolve the report's `head_sha` with `git rev-parse` (or compare by prefix) before comparing, and/or require and document the full SHA in the report schema and the fork prompt.
The "way forward" text should not suggest a reset when the reported SHA already resolves to HEAD.

Provenance: task `review-loop-convergence`; notes: webster-refusal-record-batch-2.md

## From `record-batch-no-transcripts`

Imported from [issue #457](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/457).

`lyx webster record-batch` refused to attribute a batch report with "zero new fork transcripts since the previous batch boundary", although the batch's fork had delivered a report.

Refusal text (paths trimmed):

```
webster: batch 01-carry-over-write's report could not be attributed: zero new fork transcripts since the previous batch boundary — the batch was never forked (or its transcript is not on this machine: fork transcripts are machine-local, so a crash window resumed on a different machine cannot re-attribute its report); report archived to _lyx/webster/reports/01-carry-over-write-<timestamp>.yaml; way forward: lyx webster begin-batch 01 re-drives the batch
```

Why this is abnormal: a report existed for the batch, so work was done, yet attribution found no fork transcript.
Possible causes to check: the transcript boundary advanced past the fork's transcript (for example a repeated `record-batch` or `begin-batch` for the same batch), or the fork's transcript was not located.
The refusal archived the report and told the operator to re-drive the whole batch, which discards finished work; a second refusal on the same batch followed (see the head_sha issue filed alongside this one).

What to do: find out why the transcript count was zero on a batch that was forked, and make `record-batch` idempotent or recoverable for an already-attributed batch instead of forcing a re-drive.

Provenance: task `review-loop-convergence`; notes: webster-refusal-record-batch.md

## From `plan-gate-done-cards`

Imported from [issue #463](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/463).

Seen 2026-10-08 in `shuttle-send`, following #462: the hub moved a run blocked at Publish back with `lyx loom goto --to Plan-Bouncer`, so Plan-Review would raise an uncarried parent decision against the plan.

- The plan gate validates every card against HEAD, so cards 1-10, which Webster had already run, all failed (`create-already-exists`, `glyph-not-found`, `path-missing`, `caller-uncovered`); the fixer could clear them only by retiring or rewriting done cards.
- The fixer added follow-up cards 11 and 12 with Card Index lines, but `lyx webster rebaseline --card 11 --card 12` refused: "00-overview.md changed and this run recorded no overview frame", because the run's webster record predates overview-frame tracking. Its only way forward, `lyx webster reset --to start`, would re-run all ten done cards.
- `goto` from Plan-Bouncer cannot reach Webster, so there is no route past the plan gate once the plan holds done cards.

The hub restored the recorded plan and will fix the defect forward on the task branch at Publish.

Expected: a plan gate after Webster began judges only cards after the last begun batch (done cards are history, not targets), and a webster record without an overview frame accepts a Card-Index-only change, or records the frame lazily.

## From `merriam-fixed-context-calibrate`

From webster-dead-ends PR-Gate (2026-10-08), moved out of `binary-change-and-rules` at its Discussion.

`merriamFixedContext` (`internal/websterengine/merriambase.go`) is a constant from one measurement of the system prompt and tools, so the computed Merriam base drifts silently as Claude Code changes.
A calibrate step in `tools/tokencount` re-measures it.

entries.title: Spawn audit log: every process lyx starts is recorded and traceable
entries.brief: One recorded launch path and a hub-wide spawn log with owner, argv and resource use, plus a sampler and a summary verb, so a process storm can be traced after a crash
entries.body:
## Seen

On 2026-10-08 the operator's machine froze and needed a hard reset at about 20:12 CEST while four runs were in flight.
`sar` shows about 800 process starts per second between 19:50 and 20:00, about 500 more live processes by 20:10,
and the user slice at its 16 GiB `MemoryHigh` with swap full, so reclaim thrashed (8366 major faults/s, 768 MB/s reads).
Only about 15 claude sessions and 9 subagents started in that window, and nothing in lyx's logs says what else started the processes or which run, strand or command owned them.
The operator has seen an earlier storm of 100+ claude panes in reed, and could not trace that one either.

## Idea

Every process lyx starts goes through one recorded launch path that appends an audit line to a hub-wide spawn log:
time, pid, parent pid, the lyx command and trace id that started it, hub, run slug, strand name, executable and argv,
and on exit the duration, exit status, peak RSS and bytes read and written (from `rusage` and `/proc/<pid>/io`).
This covers tmux servers, sessions and panes, claude launches, git, and `go build`/`go test` in verify gates.
A sampler, such as the reed watchdog, also records per-strand process-tree counts and memory every few seconds,
so the state just before a freeze survives a reboot.
`lyx` gains a read verb that summarises the log by minute, run, strand and executable, so a storm can be traced to its source after the fact.

entries.title: Configurable file log level in logger.yaml
entries.brief: Trace files carry only high-level messages and logger.yaml sets no level; add a file log level so most of lyx can be traced on demand
entries.body:
## Seen

The trace files written for each lyx invocation hold only high-level messages, and `_lyx/config/logger.yaml` sets only retention (`trace_retention_count`, `trace_retention_days`).
The file log has no configurable level, so after the 2026-10-08 crash the traces could not show what lyx's subcommands did.
Activity-ranked pruning also left the per-minute invocation counts incomplete.

## Idea

`logger.yaml` gains a `level` key (error, warn, info, debug) for the file trace, independent of the `-v` console verbosity, with info as the default.
Every engine logs its decisions and external calls at info or debug, so raising the level makes most of what lyx does traceable without a rebuild.
The spawn audit stays always on, whatever the level, because it cannot be turned on after a crash.

entries.title: Gate test scope: which gate runs which tier, bounded hub-wide
entries.brief: Card gate tests only its own packages at tier 1, tier 2 per batch and at the plan verify, a hub-wide slot lock for gate test runs, guarded publish_verify
entries.body:
## Seen

Before the 2026-10-08 crash, Webster implementer forks ran `go build ./... && go test ./...` plus `go test -tags integration` on their packages every 20 to 60 seconds.
That is the card gate command `cardGateCommand` derives (`internal/websterengine/cardgate.go`), run once per card.
Gates, forks, the orch and hub fix agents built and tested with no hub-wide bound, and with four runs in flight the user slice reached its 16 GiB `MemoryHigh` and the machine froze.
From `test-tiers-hardening`: the Webster-Burler round gate compiles the `tmux` tier and never runs it, so a tier 3 defect surfaces only at Publish; a task can empty its own `publish_verify` in the pair's `landing.yaml`; no gate runs the `llm` tier.

## Goal

- The card gate runs tier 1 for the card's own packages only: no `go build ./... && go test ./...` over the module and no tier 2.
- Tier 2 runs once per batch for the batch's packages, and in full at the plan verify, Publish and Finalize.
- Tier 3 stays at Publish; Discussion decides, against its cost, whether the round gate runs an impacted-set tier 3 pass.
- The `llm` tier stays by hand, and `pattern/PATTERN-test-speed.md` says so as a decision.
- A hub-wide slot lock (an OS file lock per slot, slot count in config) bounds concurrent gate test runs, each run caps `-p`, and the wait is logged and shown in status.
- The webster stencils tell each fork which packages it may test, and spawned agents are refused a raw full-module `go test` or `go build ./...`.
- A pair's own config cannot empty `publish_verify`.
- `pattern/PATTERN-test-speed.md`'s gate table and CLAUDE.md's push rule match the new gates in the same commit.
- The comment lint (`lyx loom lint-comments`, `internal/loomcli/lintcomments.go`) breaks only at a comma before a coordinating conjunction whose clause has its own subject and verb, not at every comma-plus-conjunction, so reviewers stop judging the clause-boundary rule by hand.
- A Burler reviewer's range covers what the gate failed on: when Publish failed on a defect that arrived through the merge of main, the round after a goto reads that merge and the failure, not only `git diff $(git merge-base main HEAD)..HEAD`.
- Build on the card gate as `plan-gate-checks` left it: keep its `go -C <module>` split for nested modules when narrowing to the card's own packages, and update `cardgate_test.go`.
- The plan gate's `caller-uncovered` check now runs `go list` with export data (up to 3 minutes, cgo grammars on a cold cache) on every plan-gate pass; it takes a slot of the hub-wide lock like any other gate build.

entries.title: Lighter test suite: measured tiers, cheap tmux fixtures, no lingering children
entries.brief: Measure each tier, non-login shells and shared servers in tier 3, lyx built once, no background gc in fixtures (#472), a no-tmux scan for tiers 1-2
entries.body:
## Seen

On 2026-10-08 the integration tier dominated CPU during a Publish verify (`fabricengine.test` alone at 145%), and in the 53 hours before the crash tmux started 9,022 servers and 32,375 panes, nearly all from tier 3 tests, each pane a login shell that sources the operator's profile.
Tests in four packages link the `lyx` binary with cgo on their own, and `TestLoomResumeReconcilesTheHubConfigBeforeArming` flakes on `t.TempDir` cleanup because a git child, most likely a detached auto-gc, still writes into the fixture's object store (#472).

## Goal

- A measurement of every tier per package (time, CPU, peak memory, process count) with `cmd/testtiming`, on a quiet machine, before and after.
- Tier 3 panes run a non-login shell, and tests share one tmux server per package where isolation allows.
- `lyx` is built once per test run and reused across packages.
- Git fixture repositories are reused instead of built per test (operator, 2026-10-10): today most tests build their own repos and hubs through `gitkit` (about 1,400 calls, each spawning git) and tear them down again.
  A fixture shape is built once per package (or per test binary) and shared by every test that only reads it; a test that writes gets a cheap copy of the prepared fixture, not a fresh build.
  Tests that share one fixture must not see each other's writes, so Discussion decides per fixture which tests can share it as is and which need a copy.
  Measured 2026-10-10 on a loaded machine (four runs in flight): one git process costs about 1.3 ms to spawn, a minimal repo (init, config, one commit) about 9 ms, a `cp -a` of a ready repo about 2 ms; `go test -tags integration ./internal/fabricengine/` ran 631 tests in 26.5 s and spawned 50,045 git processes, about 80 per test.
- lyx's own code spawns far fewer git processes for lookups (operator, 2026-10-10).
  In the same `fabricengine` run, by subcommand: `rev-parse` 18,825 (38%), `worktree` 7,299, `commit` and `add` 6,227, `diff` 2,628, `clone` 2,279, `config` 2,092, `push` 1,620, the rest about 9,000.
  Most `rev-parse` calls are lookups (top level, HEAD, git dir, common dir) that can be read from `.git` in-process or cached for the process's life, in `internal/gitrepo`, `internal/gitexec` and `internal/lyxcwd`; that speeds up every `lyx` command, not only the tests.
  The run cannot split fixture calls from calls by the code under test, since both run in the test binary; the measurement goal above splits them first.
- Fixture repositories never auto-gc in the background, and every test waits for the git and lyx children it starts before its cleanup.
- A scan keeps tier 1 and tier 2 free of tmux.
- A static scan enforces `PATTERN-shuttle-stop`: `RemoveStrand` on a shuttle run's strand appears only in `shuttleengine` and the exceptions the entry names (`loomcli`'s removal of the loom driver's own strand, `orchcli`'s removal of the orch strand); the PR-Gate review of `shuttle-send` found the entry false against `orchcli` with nothing to catch it.

entries.title: Git robustness: stale pack index, background gc, network timeouts, reused slugs
entries.brief: Reindex-and-retry for every go-git call, no auto-gc under a live step, timeouts on git network calls, batten refuses a done slug, bounded HeadContains
entries.body:
## Goal

- `object not found` (#468): the reindex-and-retry of `lookupObjectRetrying` covers every object-resolving go-git call in one place, `Status()` in `internal/gitrepo/worktree.go` (`UntrackedFiles`, `WorktreeChangedFiles`), tree walks and diffs included, with a regression test: build the pack index, commit with the CLI, `git repack -d` and `git prune-packed`, then call `UntrackedFiles`.
- The hub's shared object store stays below the auto-gc threshold, or auto-gc runs at known points, so no background repack lands under a live step.
- Every git network call (push, fetch) has a timeout, so a batten run never hangs after a laptop sleep.
- `batten run` on a slug whose earlier run is done refuses by name instead of reporting ok and doing nothing.
- `gitrepo.HeadContains` answers ancestry with a merge-base or a bounded walk instead of walking the whole history on every source-ahead seed pass.

The merged notes keep their own Seen sections below.

## From `merge-in-object-not-found`

Imported from [issue #468](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/468).

## Seen

Run `binary-change-and-rules`, Publish, 2026-10-08T18:41Z (trace `trace-20261008T184138Z-82c70335c18c4f83-634197.log` in the task worktree).
After `fabric: mutation kind=merge_staged` and a conflict agent finishing `done`, Publish failed with:

`landingshed: Publish: merge-in against parent branch "main": mergeresolve: list untracked files (attempt 1): fabricengine: list untracked files: gitrepo: worktree status: object not found`

The worktree was left mid-merge with `internal/battencli/wire.go` unmerged (UU) and every merged path staged.
The driver's repair re-step then stopped `blocked` on "the task worktree has uncommitted changes before the merge-in", naming the staged merge itself.
`git fsck --connectivity-only` on the pair was clean, so the object exists for git; the failure is in lyx's own worktree status read during a merge.
The machine had been hard-reset about 30 minutes earlier; that may or may not matter.

## Workaround

The orch ran `lyx fabric merge --abort` in the task worktree and `lyx loom resume`, so Publish redoes the merge-in from a clean tree.

## Expected

The untracked-file listing works mid-merge, or a failed merge-in aborts its own staged merge before refusing, so the run never halts on its own leftover merge, and the dirty-tree refusal names `lyx fabric merge --abort` when a merge is in progress.

## Root cause (orch investigation, 2026-10-08)

lyx's cached go-git handle read a stale pack index after an automatic `git gc` repacked the shared object store mid-step.
The new pack `pack-4160613d…` landed at 20:42:06 CEST while the conflict agent ran, and HEAD `64df647cf` and its tree then existed only in that pack, so the handle's index missed them and their loose copies were gone.
`internal/gitrepo/doc.go` already documents this failure, and `lookupObjectRetrying` handles it with a pack fingerprint check, `storer.Reindex()` and one retry, but the go-git `Status()` calls in `internal/gitrepo/worktree.go` (`UntrackedFiles`, `WorktreeChangedFiles`) bypass that wrapper.
The hard reset was not the cause: the pack was written 30 minutes after it and `git fsck` is clean.

## Fix

Apply the reindex-and-retry in one place that every object-resolving go-git call goes through, `Status()`, tree walks and diffs included, and add a regression test: build the index, commit with the CLI, `git repack -d` and `git prune-packed`, then call `UntrackedFiles`.

## From `shared-store-auto-gc`

## Seen

The hub's shared object store (`loomyard/.git`, used by the prime and every pair) holds about 8,450 loose objects, above git's default `gc.auto` threshold of 6,700.
They survive each repack, most likely because they are unreferenced and kept until the two-week prune expiry, so nearly every commit, merge or fetch in any worktree starts a background auto-gc.
On 2026-10-08 new packs appeared at 16:40, 18:07, 19:34, 19:52, 20:00 and 20:42, and the 20:42 one broke a Publish merge-in (#468).

## Idea

lyx keeps the shared store below the auto-gc threshold, for example by pruning unreferenced loose objects at landing, or sets `gc.auto` for the hub's store so repacks run at known points rather than under a live step.

## From `git-network-timeout`

Imported from [issue #458](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/458).

## What happened

A `lyx batten run review-lens-fan` began a best-effort status push to the weft remote at 14:11:21; the laptop hibernated four seconds later.
After resume the push hung on a dead HTTPS connection (`git send-pack` in `futex_do_wait`) for 2.5 hours, and the batten run sat at Run-Shed without starting the child loom, with no notice to the parent.
Killing the `git push` let batten log `status push failed, next transition will catch up` and go on.

## Expected

Git network calls from lyx (push and fetch, best-effort or not) run under a timeout, or with `http.lowSpeedLimit`/`http.lowSpeedTime` set, so a dead connection fails within minutes and the best-effort path takes over.


## From `batten-reused-slug`

Imported from [issue #447](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/447).

Seen: `lyx batten run webster-recovery --window` returned `{"existing":false,"ok":true,...}` and opened a window, but no pair was created and no loom run started.
`_lyx/shed/webster-recovery/status.json` held a batten run from 2026-10-02 for an earlier task of the same slug, in state `done` at Worktree-Teardown, so the new run read that status as finished.
The operator noticed only because no VS Code window opened.

Expected (operator, 2026-10-08): a slug whose task is done and pruned from the board is free, and a new task with the same slug runs as a fresh run.
A finished run's status must not stand in the way: it is archived or dropped once its task is done, so `batten run` for the new task starts at Worktree-Create.

## Proposal

- `batten run` on a slug whose status is terminal and done treats the slug as free: it archives or drops the old `_lyx/shed/<slug>/` and starts at Worktree-Create.
  A halted or failed status stays, since it is meant to be resumed.
- Removing finished runs' status directories is batten's own cleanup verb, which the repo-wide cleanup command in note `lyx-cleanup` calls.
  The board never touches shed state: `lyx board prune` stays board-only.
- A running batten run's directory is never removed, so the cleanup skips any slug whose status is not terminal.

Workaround: the task was renamed to `webster-dead-ends`.

## From `headcontains-full-walk`

## Seen

The PR-Gate review of `binary-change-and-rules` (PR #469) found that `gitrepo.HeadContains` (`internal/gitrepo/blobread.go`) walks HEAD's whole history through go-git whenever a seed pass finds a source-ahead stencil.
In a long-history repository that cost lands on every command until the pair syncs with main.

## Idea

Answer the ancestry question with a merge-base or a walk bounded by commit date or depth instead of a full history walk.

entries.title: Publish and loom recovery: a fix route from Publish, resume past its own merge, clean re-steps
entries.brief: A blocked Publish hands its failure to a fixer, resume survives its own staged merge, no false config warning at Finalize, re-step and decision-author fixes
entries.body:
## Goal

- A blocked Publish has a route that hands its failure to a fixer as a finding (#462), so the hub never falls back to `goto Plan-Bouncer` for one fix.
- `lyx loom resume` at Publish recovers from the staged merge-in a failed merge-in left behind (#471), and the dirty-tree refusal names `lyx fabric merge --abort` when a merge is in progress.
- Finalize warns only of per-worktree config changes the task made, never of changes that came from main.
- A loom re-step is not refused while a stopped review strand's run dir is younger than 3 minutes (#452).
- A plan agent cannot record a decision as `--by parent` (#453).

The merged notes keep their own Seen sections below.

## From `publish-fix-route`

Imported from [issue #462](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/462).

Seen 2026-10-08 in `shuttle-send`: Publish blocked three times on the same `publish_verify` failure (three `//go:build tmux` loomcli tests), and the two fix routes the hub has from a blocked Publish never reached the defect.

The defect arrived through the merge of main (reed-view typed `/color` raw into the pane), so it is outside the task's diff.

- `lyx loom decision add --by parent` plus `lyx loom goto --to Webster-Burler`: the Webster-Review rubric measures against the plan, not the decision record, and the reviewer reads only `git diff $(git merge-base main HEAD)..HEAD`, so both rounds approved with unrelated NITs and the decision was never acted on.
- The Webster-Burler verify gate compiles the `tmux` tier and never runs it (`internal/loomshed/doc.go`), so the fixer never saw the failing tests either.
- `lyx loom reject` works only at PR-Gate or PR-Rework, and `goto` refuses PR-Rework from Publish because it lies past the current row, so the hub cannot hand the failure to a fixer as a finding.

The hub fell back to `goto Plan-Bouncer`, so Plan-Review raises the uncarried decision against the plan, which re-runs Plan-Burler, Batchifier and Webster for one fix.

Expected: a blocked Publish (or any blocked row after Webster) has a route that hands a named finding to a fixer round, e.g. `lyx loom reject` accepted at a blocked Publish, or a Webster-Burler round that takes the publish_verify failure and post-Discussion parent decisions as its focus.

## From `publish-resume-own-merge`

Imported from [issue #471](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/471).

## What happened

After a `Publish` step failed mid merge-in (merge staged, conflict resolved by the agent, then a producer refusal), the loom driver re-stepped once.
The run then halted as `blocked` at `Publish`, anomaly `escalation-to-human`, with this reason:

`the task worktree has uncommitted changes before the merge-in: <a long list of files, plus "and 63 more">; commit or remove them on the task branch, then resume`

The listed files are the changes the staged merge-in itself brought in, not the task's own uncommitted work.

## Why it is abnormal

The merge-in precondition check treats the worktree state produced by the earlier, interrupted merge-in attempt as foreign uncommitted changes.
A re-step or resume after a partial merge-in can therefore never pass the check, and the run escalates to a human although all earlier segments (Discussion, Plan, Webster, Describe) were `done`.
The advice in the message ("commit or remove them") would either commit an unfinished merge or discard the resolution.

## What to do

- Detect an in-progress merge (`MERGE_HEAD` present, or merge-staged state recorded in the trace/history) in the `Publish` precondition and resume it, instead of applying the clean-worktree check.
- Alternatively provide a `lyx` repair verb that completes or aborts a staged merge-in, and name it in this refusal message.
- Make the loom driver's repair step aware of this state, so it does not re-step into a guaranteed refusal.

Related: the transient `object not found` report, which is what first interrupted the merge-in.

Provenance: task `binary-change-and-rules`, from `loom-halt.md` and `driver-repair-1.md`.

## From `finalize-config-warn-from-main`

Imported from [issue #450](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/450).

At Finalize, loom warns: `task branch "<slug>" changed per-worktree config files since it forked from "main": _lyx/config/batcher.yaml (base <sha>, tip <sha>); landing does not carry them to the parent branch, so re-apply each change meant for the parent on the parent's copy`.

Seen for `shuttle-state` and `plan-glyph-precision` on 2026-10-08.
In both, the pair's `batcher.yaml` was byte-identical to the prime's: the change was main's own commit (`batcher: cautious is the template default`, c0bf19c54) arriving in the pair through the weft sync, not an edit the task made.

Expected: the check compares the tip against the parent's current copy (or excludes changes the weft sync brought in), and warns only when the task's copy differs from the parent's.
As it is, the warning fires on every run that forked before a config change on main, and the hub must diff each time to rule it out.

## From `restep-young-run-dir`

Imported from [issue #452](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/452).

## What happened

After a driver repair, the re-step of the Discussion burler segment failed with a non-transient `producer` error.
The trace line: `shed: step refused kind=producer transient="" error="... probe the burler-review half: shuttle: attach: 1 candidate run dir(s) ... cannot be confirmed dead or alive (untracked or with a cleared pane binding, younger than 3m0s) ..."`.
The run dir had been left by the review strand that the previous step itself stopped.
`lyx reed status` listed no such strand, while the burler-fix strand was still live, and no fabric mutation was half-finished.
The driver's only remedy was to wait until the run dir passed the 3m age and re-step, which cost a repair round (history_length 6).

## Why it is abnormal

The strand was stopped by lyx moments earlier, so its run dir is known dead, yet the burler probe treats it as unclassifiable and refuses the step.
A refusal that resolves itself with time should be a transient error, not a `producer` error that consumes a repair.

## What to do

- Have the stop path record or clear the stopped strand's pane binding, so the probe can classify its run dir as dead immediately.
- Alternatively, report the young-run-dir refusal as transient so the loom retries instead of halting for repair.

Provenance: task `plan-glyph-precision`; note `driver-repair-20261008-discussion-burler-2.md`.

## From `plan-agent-parent-decision`

Imported from [issue #453](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/453).

## What happened

In the `shuttle-send` run, the Plan-Write agent recorded a decision as the parent:

```
lyx loom decision add --by parent --title "PATTERN-shuttle-stop names the loom driver exception" ...
```

The Plan role writes its own output files only; a design call outside the decided scope goes to the parent.
`lyx loom decision add` accepted `--by parent` from inside the plan agent's session, so the record reads as the hub's decision though the hub never made it.

## Expected

`decision add --by parent` refuses when it runs inside a lyx-spawned agent session other than the parent's, or the Plan stencil's deny hooks block it, so a plan agent's scope call reaches the parent as an escalation or an open question in the plan.

## Context

The decision itself was narrow and the hub would have taken it (it names loomcli's raw removal of the loom driver's strand as an exception in the new PATTERN entry).
The defect is the forged authorship, not the content.

entries.title: Webster state across replans: goto to Plan, late plan reviews, rebaseline clarity
entries.brief: Webster stays consistent after a goto to Plan or a late Plan-Review round, rebaseline names its fallback, one-call head_sha check, verify-module splits at || and |
entries.body:
## Goal

- A `lyx loom goto` back to Plan after Webster started leaves webster state consistent, so Webster never hard-fails on a plan fingerprint mismatch (#466).
- A Plan-Review round after the plan is implemented is not dispatched as a fix round that edits the plan webster recorded (#465).
- Rebaseline logs and names the silent overview-frame fallback when the baseline copy has no parseable Card Index.
- `commitsNamedBy` classifies every `head_sha` prefix candidate in one `git cat-file --batch-check` call.
- `verify-nested-module` (`crossModuleCommands` in `internal/planparser/verifymodule.go`) splits a verify chain at `||` and `|` as well.

The merged notes keep their own Seen sections below.

## From `goto-plan-stale-webster`

Imported from [issue #466](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/466).

## What happened

A loom run completed the Plan, Batchifier and Webster rows, then the Publish row went stuck and the run routed back (`goto`) to `Plan-Bouncer` several times.
The Plan loop edited the plan, and `Batchifier` re-ran and finished (`done`).
The next `Webster` step then halted the run as `failed` with anomaly `producer-hard-failure`:

```
webster: on-disk plan fingerprint does not match this run's recorded state: on-disk plan fingerprint e5774b7e... does not match this run's recorded fingerprint c14834a3...; the plan changed since state.json was created; way forward: 00-overview.md changed and is never rebaselined; restore it with "lyx webster restore-plan", or 1) lyx webster reset --to start; 2) re-step the Webster row
```

The run had 49 history entries when it halted.

## Why this is abnormal

The loom's own routing sent the run back through Plan after Webster had already created `state.json`, and then re-ran Webster against that stale state.
The recorded fingerprint can only match if the plan is untouched, so a legitimate Plan-loop edit made the next Webster step fail by construction.
Neither the `goto` to Plan nor the re-run `Batchifier` row reset or rebaselined webster state, so the failure was foreseeable from the recipe's own wiring rather than an operator or task-code error.
The error text offers manual recovery (`lyx webster restore-plan`, or `lyx webster reset --to start` and re-step), which a driver could have applied itself.

## What to do

When the loom routes back to a row upstream of Webster after Webster state exists, reset webster state (equivalent to `lyx webster reset --to start`) as part of that route, or have the Webster row detect a changed plan produced by an upstream re-run and rebaseline instead of failing.
Alternatively, make the recipe validate at the `goto` that a Plan re-entry invalidates downstream webster state.

Provenance: task slug `shuttle-send`; notes: `loom-halt.md`.

## From `plan-review-after-implemented`

Imported from [issue #465](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/465).

A Plan-Review round ran over a plan that was already approved and implemented by webster.
The review gained findings, but the fixer's only write surface was the plan, and webster could not accept a new card on this run's record.
`lyx webster rebaseline --card=[11,12]` was refused:

```
webster: the edited plan changes the cards of a batch this run already begun: 00-overview.md changed and this run recorded no overview frame, so the change cannot be confined to its Card Index; it carries the plan's integration verify and is never rebaselined; way forward: restore 00-overview.md, or 1) lyx webster reset --to start; 2) lyx webster run
```

The parent stopped all fixes mid-round, so every finding ended deferred.
The fixer also spent its orientation designing a new card that was then thrown away.

Why this is abnormal: the loom dispatches a review round whose fixes cannot land.
A frozen plan (webster already begun) makes the fix round unwinnable, and the only advertised way forward (`lyx webster reset --to start`) discards the implemented work.
The run records no overview frame, so a legitimate edit to the overview's Card Index cannot be confined and is refused outright.

What to do:
- Skip the fix-round dispatch, or tell the round prompt up front that the plan is frozen, when the run's webster record has begun a batch.
- Record an overview frame when webster begins a batch, so a Card Index change can be confined and rebaselined.

Provenance: task `shuttle-send`; notes `burler-plan-r1.md`, `webster-refusal-rebaseline.md`.

## From `overview-frame-fallback-log`

## Seen

The PR-Gate review of `webster-record-batch` (PR #473) found that `recordedOverviewFrame` in `internal/websterengine` returns an empty frame without logging when the stored baseline copy has no parseable Card Index, so the reason a rebaseline refuses on an old record is invisible.

## Idea

Log the fallback at Info with the baseline path, and name it in the rebaseline refusal.

## From `head-sha-batch-check`

## Seen

The PR-Gate review of `webster-record-batch` (PR #473) found that `commitsNamedBy` in `internal/websterengine/gitwrap.go` runs one `git cat-file -t` per object a short `head_sha` prefix names, and a 4-character prefix in a large repository can name many.

## Idea

Classify every candidate in one `git cat-file --batch-check` call.

## From `verify-module-or-pipe`

## Seen

The PR-Gate review of `plan-gate-checks` (PR #475) found that `crossModuleCommands` in `internal/planparser/verifymodule.go` splits a verify chain only at `&&`, `;` and newlines, so a `go` command after `||` or a pipe is read as part of the previous segment and its module is never checked.

## Idea

Split at `||` and `|` too.


## From issue #476

Imported from [issue #476](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/476).

## What happened

A plan card required one exact sentence to be added to the `PATTERN-shuttle-stop` line in `PATTERN.md`, with nothing else changed.
With that sentence the line is 409 characters, but `internal/pattern`'s `MaxEntryLineChars` caps an entry line at 320, and `TestOverview_RealFilePassesCheck` enforces the cap.
The plan was approved anyway, so the card could not be satisfied as written.

## Why this is abnormal

The implementer had to reword the whole line.
The reviewer, checking against the card's text, raised the reword as a finding (F1) and proposed a fix that fails the plan's own verify.
That produced extra Webster-Burler rounds on a defect that was fixed in the plan, not in the code.
The plan gate (Plan-Write, Plan-Bouncer) has no check that exercises a card's verbatim PATTERN text against the entry cap.

## What to do

Add a plan-gate check: when a card prescribes verbatim text for a `PATTERN.md` entry line, compute the resulting line length and reject the card if it exceeds `MaxEntryLineChars`.
Alternatively, tell Plan-Write in its instructions to check verbatim PATTERN text against the cap before approving the card.

Provenance: task `shuttle-send`; notes `burler-webster-r1.md`, `loom-halt.md`.

entries.title: Haiku 5.5 for the light roles: driver and judge

## Seen

The operator benchmarked Haiku 5.5 on 2026-10-08 (`docs/benchmarks/haiku-5-5.md`): on one fully specified coding task it scored as well as Sonnet and Opus at medium, at a fraction of the cost, but took about twice as long and grew its context to 74–132k.

## Idea

Run the driver and the judge on Haiku 5.5 where it holds (operator, 2026-10-08: most likely only these two; the other roles stay as they are).

- Set `driver` and `judge` in `loom.yaml` to a Haiku model-spec on one trial run, and compare against a Sonnet run from the usage records: interventions by the hub, judge verdicts later overturned, and token cost.
- Keep the change only for a role whose trial shows no more interventions or overturned verdicts.

Compare the driver row of the token report per role, and the hub interventions, against the Sonnet runs before it.

## Seen in use



- 2026-10-10, `bolt-and-store`: the Haiku 5.5 driver read its prompt, summarized its rules, and ended the turn asking "Tell me when to start", although the prompt says it runs autonomously with no operator to ask.

  The Haiku drivers of `multi-llm-producer` and `daemon-wakeups`, on the same prompt, started stepping at once; a message from the orch got it going.

  The driver stencil (`contracts/stencils/shed/shed-template-driver.md`) never says "start now"; a line that reading the prompt is the go-ahead and the first turn launches the first step would close it.

entries.title: MultiLLMProducer: one producer runs a chair and its advisors as seats
entries.brief: A producer beside SingleLLMProducer that runs N agents as seats, one chair that steers and decides the outcome plus advisor-1..n, with its own internal message channel; built standalone, used by nothing yet
entries.body:
## Goal

`MultiLLMProducer` in `internal/shedadapters`, beside `SingleLLMProducer`: one producer runs N agents in one step, each in a strand of its own.
It is built standalone and proven by its own tests and a test recipe: no recipe row, Burler or Discussion uses it in this task (operator, 2026-10-08).

## Terms (operator, 2026-10-08)

- A **seat** is one agent in a `MultiLLMProducer`.
- Exactly one seat is the **`chair`**: its turn end, outputs and gates decide the step's outcome, as a single agent's do today, and a message sent to the producer goes to the chair.
- Every other seat is an **advisor**, named `advisor-1`, `advisor-2` and so on, in every `MultiLLMProducer`.
- Strands are named after the seat, such as `ly:<slug>:discussion-chair` and `ly:<slug>:discussion-advisor-1`.
- Not "master": that is Webster's `Master`.

## Seats: one table says what goes where

Burler's round today wires six stencils (two orchestrator templates, three step files, a focus directive) plus per-segment rubrics and the Bouncer's judge stencils through Go code spread over several packages.
A `MultiLLMProducer` declares its seats in one place (the recipe row or one Go table):

- the seat's name (`chair` or `advisor-<n>`);
- exactly one stencil per seat, the only prompt that agent gets; shared building blocks are included from it by name;
- a model key in config;
- inputs (files and markers the seat is given) and outputs (files it writes); an advisor's output is the chair's input.

A test pins that every seat's stencil markers are filled (`stencil.Fill` already refuses an empty marker) and that every advisor output is the chair's input.

## Messaging

This first version carries its own internal message channel between seats; `creel` is not used and comes later on its own (operator, 2026-10-08).
The chair always steers: a message to the producer goes to the chair, and advisors reach the chair through the channel.
Whether advisors may message each other is decided in Discussion.

## Shape

Inside one producer, not parallel shed producers (operator, 2026-10-07): shed sees one step with one outcome, and the seats are invisible to it.
A single-agent producer is the case N = 1; whether `SingleLLMProducer` itself becomes that case is decided in Discussion, without changing any recipe row.

## Open for Discussion

- What an advisor's failure or hang does to the step.
- How the producer knows an advisor is done (the session-state model from `shuttle-state`).
- How the seats' strands are laid out until `reed-layout-shares` lands.

## Out

- Burler on `MultiLLMProducer` and Discussion-Write on it are their own tasks.
- `creel`, and the even layout (`reed-layout-shares`).
